title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad (INT8/FP8/BF16)
content:
Objective:
Short notes and breadcrumbs while triaging NaNs / quality regressions observed after INT8/FP8 experiments on Llama-like models. This is a personal scratchpad — lots of hypotheses, commands I ran, and tiny repro steps. Intended to be messy.

Summary so far:
- Started seeing intermittent NaNs during generation in our optimized INT8 runtime when switching from BF16 baseline. Failures appear more frequent on long-context runs (>1024 tokens) and with KV-cache reuse across batches.\n- FP8 experiments (experimental quant path) also triggered some NaNs but with different stack traces.\n- BF16 baseline (pytorch native, amp) is stable.\n- Repro is *non-deterministic* but I can increase probability of hitting NaN by using: long sequences, batch_size>1, enable_kv_sharing=true.

Environments tested:
- docker image: redwood/serving-runtime:canary-2026-03-08
- pytorch 2.2.0+cu118 (built-in)
- bitsandbytes 0.40.0 (for int8 matmul)
- CUDA 11.8 kernel drivers
- kernels: custom_fused_attention v2 (we swapped v1->v2 on 2026-03-05)
- model: llama-2-13b (hf checkpoint converted with our export script)

Fast repro command (high-probability):
- python tests/repro/run_local_repro.py --model out/llama-2-13b-int8 --quant int8 --batch 4 --seq_len 1536 --enable_kv_sharing true --seed 42
Observed output: repeated lines like:
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of bounds or invalid value detected (NaN) at aten::addmm or at aten::matmul (stack trace differs between int8 path and fp8 path)
- GPU logs: NDEBUG: kernel failed: compute_SM80, grid=(..), block=(..), status=INVALID
- sometimes we see: Check failed: !isnan(x) at quantized_gemm.cu:176

Commands and small experiments run (notes inline):
1) Re-run without KV sharing:
- python tests/repro/run_local_repro.py --model out/llama-2-13b-int8 --quant int8 --batch 4 --seq_len 1536 --enable_kv_sharing false
- Result: runs clean ~20/20. Hypothesis: KV cache path interacting with quantized matmuls or cache indexing.

2) Reduce batch size to 1 with KV sharing on:
- batch 1 + enable_kv_sharing true -> still occasionally NaN but much less frequent. So batch dimension contributes (maybe packing/transpose bug).

3) Swap fused attention kernel back to v1:
- rolled runtime to custom_fused_attention v1 (git abcd123 revert)
- Re-run repro -> NaNs dropped to near-zero. Suggests kernel change interacts with quantized path.

4) FP8 path (experimental):
- python tests/repro/run_local_repro.py --model out/llama-2-13b-fp8 --quant fp8 --batch 4 --seq_len 1536
- Observed NaN with stack: aten::native_layer_norm -> aten::linear -> quant_matmul_fp8.cu
- But when running with --disable_kernel_fusion flag, FP8 run is stable. So fusion + FP8 likely bad.

5) Quick check: Is quantization scale overflow happening?
- Inserted debug prints in quantize_weight() to log scale values on first forward. Observed a few extremely large scales (~1e6) only on v2 fused kernel path -> indicates upstream accumulation without clamp.

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Kernel fusion v2 has an index/stride bug when tensors are quantized (INT8/FP8) which leads to reading out-of-bounds or uninitialized memory -> NaN. (evidence: v1 -> stable, v2 -> NaN)
- H2: Batching + KV-sharing interaction causes incorrect reshaping/transpose for packed int8 blocks leading to wrong scale application. (evidence: batch>1 higher repro)
- H3: FP8 quant path uses a different accumulation precision in fused kernels and we hit overflow in accumulation without proper FP8->higher-precision accumulation fallback. (evidence: extreme scale values; disable fusion -> stable)
- H4: Softmax/attention numerics not stable when quantized with our approximations for large seq_len; when combined with fused kernel reorderings this amplifies to NaN.

Artifacts / quick traces:
- Example stack (INT8 run):
  File "src/runtime/quantized_gemm.cu", line 176, in quantized_gemm
  Check failed: !isnan(x)
  CUDA kernel log: device[0] SM80 kernel failed status INVALID
- Example stack (FP8 run):
  File "src/ops/fused_attention.cu", line 512, in fused_attn_forward
  aten::native_layer_norm -> aten::linear -> quant_matmul_fp8.cu:89 -> __global__ fp8_gemm_kernel

Reproducer mini-test (Python unit) I added: tests/unit/test_quant_kv_repro.py (local only) that toggles kernel flags and runs a short forward/backward on a toy transformer block with random inputs and sets torch.manual_seed(42). This test passes 95% when using v1 kernels, fails ~35% with v2.

Notes about mitigation checked so far:
- Add guard clamping of scale values after quantize weight (quick patch) -> reduces frequency but does not eliminate. Suggests symptom, not root cause.
- Disable fusion for FP8 in production until root cause triaged (temporary fix).
- Revert fused-attention v2 for the int8 code path only -> major perf regression but stable.

Next steps (short):
- Evan to add comprehensive index/stride unit tests for fused kernel v2 by Mar 14 (blocked: Evan OOO Thursdays).
- Priya to run a matrix of long-seq/batch combinations on dedicated GPU (r7) to gather flaky repro logs and exact failure probabilities. Add GPU core dumps when status INVALID.
- I will instrument quantize_weight and quant_matmul kernels to record first N scale values and first N indices accessed for suspect batches and upload to S3: s3://redwood-debug/quant-nan/2026-03-12/
- Attempt to reproduce on a different CUDA version/machine (test cuda12 on a devbox) to rule out driver issues.

Debugging checklist (what I'm going to try next):
- [ ] Reproduce with deterministic seeds + torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True to see if that changes behavior.
- [ ] Run with memcheck and address-sanitizer on the fused kernel in CI (slow but will reveal OOBs).
- [ ] Add asserts to kernel boundary checks (index guards) and run repro.
- [ ] Bisect custom_fused_attention v1->v2 commits to find the specific change that introduced NaN (start at commit 0f9a2 -> 8b3c1).
- [ ] Try converting weights with per-channel vs per-tensor scale quantization to see difference.
- [ ] Run with reduced sequence length and artificially high token probability to stress attention softmax numerics.

Random notes / breadcrumbs:
- Slack channel: #quant-nan (thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02Q9XXXX/p1678889)
- Related older ticket: JIRA-INF-1210 (int8 matmul weirdness on small batches, 2025-11)
- Quick local artifact: /tmp/quant_debug/trace_2026-03-12.tar.gz (contains nvprof traces and kernel logs)

If I get a solid minimal reproducer kernel-level (C++/CUDA), next step is to open a high-priority PR that adds extra index checks + a small microbench to reproduce the failing indexing pattern. If that shows failure, we fix index math; if it doesn't, dig into accumulation precision.

If anyone reading: please ping in #quant-nan or DM me (Maya) if you have ideas. Will update this doc as I make progress.

End of scratchpad entry (2026-03-12).
